{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0182VoMJuTTs9Pvcf2NCLJEf","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its\n# exit code and output as the score. The interface check is separate from the conformance run so\n# that a missing or non-executable program and a genuine conformance failure are distinguishable\n# in the evidence. The program path is the harness's only knowledge of the implementation\n# language; the harness itself is language-neutral.\n#\n# The suite runs unfiltered: no --pattern, no --number, no selector of any kind. spec_tests.py\n# exits with failed + errored, so exit 0 means the complete CommonMark 0.31.2 suite passed.\nset -eu\n\nif [ ! -x ./commonmark ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./commonmark at the application root.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named commonmark that reads UTF-8 Markdown on stdin\" >&2\n    echo \"and writes HTML to stdout.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# spec_tests.py imports cmark and normalize as siblings, so the staged directory has to be on the\n# import path. The program is passed absolute because the runner spawns it from its own cwd.\nPYTHONPATH=\"$PWD/sources${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}\"\nexport PYTHONPATH\n\nset +e\noutput=$(python3 sources/spec_tests.py --program \"$PWD/commonmark\" --spec sources/spec.txt 2>&1)\nstatus=$?\nset -e\n\nprintf '%s\\n' \"$output\"\n\n# The runner exits with failed + errored, which a shell truncates modulo 256: exactly 256 or 512\n# failures would exit 0 and read as a pass. The harness therefore confirms the tally rather than\n# trusting the status alone, and reports a clean run only when both agree. This is the scoring\n# instrument reading its own instrument; the acceptance check above it still asserts nothing but\n# this script's exit code.\nif [ \"$status\" -ne 0 ]; then\n    exit 1\nfi\nif ! printf '%s\\n' \"$output\" | grep -q '0 failed, 0 errored, 0 skipped'; then\n    echo \"error: conformance runner exited 0 but did not report a clean unfiltered suite.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n----\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n\nimport sys\nfrom difflib import unified_diff\nimport argparse\nimport re\nimport json\nfrom cmark import CMark\nfrom normalize import normalize_html\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Run cmark tests.')\n    parser.add_argument('-p', '--program', dest='program', nargs='?', default=None,\n            help='program to test')\n    parser.add_argument('-s', '--spec', dest='spec', nargs='?', default='spec.txt',\n            help='path to spec')\n    parser.add_argument('-P', '--pattern', dest='pattern', nargs='?',\n            default=None, help='limit to sections matching regex pattern')\n    parser.add_argument('--library-dir', dest='library_dir', nargs='?',\n            default=None, help='directory containing dynamic library')\n    parser.add_argument('--no-normalize', dest='normalize',\n            action='store_const', const=False, default=True,\n            help='do not normalize HTML')\n    parser.add_argument('-d', '--dump-tests', dest='dump_tests',\n            action='store_const', const=True, default=False,\n            help='dump tests in JSON format')\n    parser.add_argument('--debug-normalization', dest='debug_normalization',\n            action='store_const', const=True,\n            default=False, help='filter stdin through normalizer for testing')\n    parser.add_argument('-n', '--number', type=int, default=None,\n            help='only consider the test with the given number')\n    parser.add_argument('--track', metavar='path',\n            help='track which test cases pass/fail in the given JSON file and only report changes')\n    args = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:])\n\ndef out(str):\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(str.encode('utf-8')) \n\ndef print_test_header(test):\n    out(\"Example %d (lines %d-%d) %s\\n\" % (test['example'], test['start_line'], test['end_line'], test['section']))\n\ndef do_test(test, normalize, prev_result):\n    [retcode, actual_html_bytes, err] = cmark.to_html(test['markdown'])\n    if retcode != 0:\n        if prev_result != 'error':\n            print_test_header(test)\n            out(\"program returned error code %d\\n\" % retcode)\n            sys.stdout.buffer.write(err)\n        return 'error'\n\n    expected_html = test['html']\n\n    try:\n        actual_html = actual_html_bytes.decode('utf-8')\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:\n        if prev_result != 'fail':\n            print_test_header(test)\n            out(test['markdown'] + '\\n')\n            out(\"Unicode error: \" + str(e) + '\\n')\n            out(\"Expected: \" + repr(expected_html) + '\\n')\n            out(\"Got:      \" + repr(actual_html_bytes) + '\\n')\n            out('\\n')\n        return 'fail'\n\n    if normalize:\n        actual_html = normalize_html(actual_html) + '\\n'\n        expected_html = normalize_html(expected_html) + '\\n'\n\n    if actual_html != expected_html:\n        if prev_result != 'fail':\n            print_test_header(test)\n            out(test['markdown'] + '\\n')\n            expected_html_lines = expected_html.splitlines(True)\n            actual_html_lines = actual_html.splitlines(True)\n            for diffline in unified_diff(expected_html_lines, actual_html_lines,\n                            \"expected HTML\", \"actual HTML\"):\n                out(diffline)\n            out('\\n')\n        return 'fail'\n----\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n\nfrom ctypes import CDLL, c_char_p, c_long, c_int\nfrom subprocess import *\nimport platform\nimport os\n\ndef pipe_through_prog(prog, text):\n    p1 = Popen(prog.split(), stdout=PIPE, stdin=PIPE, stderr=PIPE)\n    [result, err] = p1.communicate(input=text.encode('utf-8'))\n    return [p1.returncode, result, err]\n\ndef use_library(lib, text):\n    textbytes = text.encode('utf-8')\n    textlen = len(textbytes)\n    return [0, lib(textbytes, textlen, 0), '']\n\nclass CMark:\n    def __init__(self, prog=None, library_dir=None):\n        self.prog = prog\n        if prog:\n            self.to_html = lambda x: pipe_through_prog(prog, x)\n        else:\n            sysname = platform.system()\n            if sysname == 'Darwin':\n                libname = \"libcmark.dylib\"\n            elif sysname == 'Windows':\n                libname = \"cmark.dll\"\n            else:\n                libname = \"libcmark.so\"\n            if library_dir:\n                libpath = os.path.join(library_dir, libname)\n            else:\n                libpath = os.path.join(\"build\", \"src\", libname)\n            cmark = CDLL(libpath)\n            markdown = cmark.cmark_markdown_to_html\n            markdown.restype = c_char_p\n            markdown.argtypes = [c_char_p, c_long, c_int]\n            self.to_html = lambda x: use_library(markdown, The executable takes no options.\n- **Exit status:** always 0, for any input, including empty input.\n\n## Requirements\n\nPython 3.11 or later. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018AGpm13D5qnZrLuiTowbw7","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n\ndef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\n    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n----\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01So2HRseGpGY3mprxEknXhc","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\n4\tnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\n5\tunescape helper.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\t\n8\timport string\n9\t\n10\t# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\n11\tASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n12\t\n13\t\n14\tdef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n15\t    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n16\t\n17\t    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n18\t    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n19\t    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n20\t    \"\"\"\n21\t    out: list[str] = []\n22\t    index = 0\n23\t    while index < len(text):\n24\t        char = text[index]\n25\t        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n26\t            out.append(text[index + 1])\n27\t            index += 2\n28\t            continue\n29\t        out.append(char)\n30\t        index += 1\n31\t    return \"\".join(out)\n32\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f24ea800-6ae1-488e-80dd-9351d150839d","uuid":"5aebbd05-4ed7-4d23-8ed4-aeddce9ffbc4","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:16:10.582Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/entities.py","content":"\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n\ndef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\n    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n","numLines":32,"startLine":1,"totalLines":32}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01So2HRseGpGY3mprxEknXhc","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1e5qG9YngtP9cpAVQqg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01PUeeG4caxSpvhhCpjW34yC","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/entities.py","content":"\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper and the shared destination, title and info-string helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport html.entities\nimport re\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n# A named reference: `&`, a name, then `;`. The table lookup adds the semicolon back.\nNAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);\")\n# A decimal reference has 1 to 7 digits. A hexadecimal reference has `x` or `X` and 1 to 6 digits.\nDECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#([0-9]{1,7});\")\nHEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#[xX]([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6});\")\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nMAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF\n\n\ndef match_reference(text: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded text of the character reference at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    Returns None when no recognized reference starts at `start`, so the `&` is literal text. An\n    unknown name, or a name without its semicolon, is not a reference.\n    \"\"\"\n    named = NAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if named is not None:\n        value = html.entities.html5.get(named.group(1) + \";\")\n        if value is None:\n            return None\n        return value, named.end()\n    decimal = DECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if decimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(decimal.group(1), 10)), decimal.end()\n    hexadecimal = HEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if hexadecimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(hexadecimal.group(1), 16)), hexadecimal.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _code_point_text(code_point: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the character for a numeric reference. Zero, surrogates and out-of-range values\n    become U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    if code_point == 0 or code_point > MAX_CODE_POINT or 0xD800 <= code_point <= 0xDFFF:\n        return REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER\n    return chr(code_point)\n\n\ndef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\n    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef unescape_and_decode(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes and character references to `text` in one left-to-right pass.\n\n    This is the shared helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. The pass is single\n    so that an escape is never read as the start of a reference: `\\\\&amp;` yields the literal text\n    `&amp;`, not `&`.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(text, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(value)\n                continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3968,"cache_read_input_tokens":39677,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3968},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f24ea800-6ae1-488e-80dd-9351d150839d","uuid":"9f2e421a-f9a5-405e-9216-69cd3bc8c31d","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:16:16.922Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1e5pxnwqfVgR8r28c7C","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01PUeeG4caxSpvhhCpjW34yC":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/entities.py","content":"\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper and the shared destination, title and info-string helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport html.entities\nimport re\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n# A named reference: `&`, a name, then `;`. The table lookup adds the semicolon back.\nNAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);\")\n# A decimal reference has 1 to 7 digits. A hexadecimal reference has `x` or `X` and 1 to 6 digits.\nDECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#([0-9]{1,7});\")\nHEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#[xX]([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6});\")\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"\\uFFFD\"\nMAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF\n\n\ndef match_reference(text: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded text of the character reference at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    Returns None when no recognized reference starts at `start`, so the `&` is literal text. An\n    unknown name, or a name without its semicolon, is not a reference.\n    \"\"\"\n    named = NAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if named is not None:\n        value = html.entities.html5.get(named.group(1) + \";\")\n        if value is None:\n            return None\n        return value, named.end()\n    decimal = DECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if decimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(decimal.group(1), 10)), decimal.end()\n    hexadecimal = HEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if hexadecimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(hexadecimal.group(1), 16)), hexadecimal.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _code_point_text(code_point: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the character for a numeric reference. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef unescape_and_decode(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes and character references to `text` in one left-to-right pass.\n\n    This is the shared helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CX9xJXWE3SLDNGakDoDq7u","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f24ea800-6ae1-488e-80dd-9351d150839d","uuid":"b7a73166-7602-4f33-9d13-0d056a505628","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:16:19.083Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py","oldString":"from mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url","newString":"from mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                out.append(raw[index:raw_html_end])\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":7,"oldLines":7,"newStart":7,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," import re"," ","-from mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION","+from mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference"," from mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url"," "," # The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01CX9xJXWE3SLDNGakDoDq7u","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01VhdzrwawERBnHf8D18MJj6","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f24ea800-6ae1-488e-80dd-9351d150839d","uuid":"88c2ac46-ee2d-4fdb-984a-3c4c27e54913","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:16:21.678Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py","oldString":"        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))","newString":"        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(escape_html(value))\n                continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                out.append(raw[index:raw_html_end])\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; Everything else is\n    escaped text.\n    \"\"\"","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                out.append(raw[index:raw_html_end])\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(escape_html(value))\n                continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":58,"oldLines":7,"newStart":58,"newLines":9,"lines":["     equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1e71cHG98yiDvfjrELG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0163MhgMQsFXxtiHtKi9SxiF","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_entities.py","content":"\"\"\"Entity and numeric character reference tests: named references from the HTML5 table, decimal\nand hexadecimal numeric references, U+FFFD replacement, decoded text as plain text, inertness in\ncode spans, and the shared `unescape_and_decode` helper for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\nEach test compares a returned string, a parsed value, or the executable's stdout bytes with its\nexact expected value. The declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import entities\nfrom mdparser.entities import match_reference, unescape_and_decode\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, data: str) -> str:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, data)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_entities_decimal_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-decimal-reference: a decimal reference decodes to the character with the bound code point.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 65\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"x &#\" + str(code_point) + \"; y\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.count(b\"&#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_entities_hex_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-hex-reference: lowercase and uppercase hexadecimal references decode to the same character.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 66\n    lower = \"&#x\" + format(code_point, \"x\") + \";\"\n    upper = \"&#X\" + format(code_point, \"X\") + \";\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, lower + \"\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, upper + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in first.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_named_ampersand(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-named-ampersand: the named ampersand reference round trips to the same escaped form.\"\"\"\n    reference = \"&amp;\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a \" + reference + \" b\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert reference in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_unknown_stays_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-unknown-stays-literal: an unknown entity name is literal text with its ampersand escaped.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"&MadeUpEntity;\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef The declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import entities\nfrom mdparser.entities import match_reference, unescape_and_decode\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, data: str) -> str:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, data)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_entities_decimal_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-decimal-reference: a decimal reference decodes to the character with the bound code point.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 65\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"x &#\" + str(code_point) + \"; y\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.count(b\"&#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_entities_hex_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-hex-reference: lowercase and uppercase hexadecimal references decode to the same character.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 66\n    lower = \"&#x\" + format(code_point, \"x\") + \";\"\n    upper = \"&#X\" + format(code_point, \"X\") + \";\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, lower + \"\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, upper + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in first.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_named_ampersand(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-named-ampersand: the named ampersand reference round trips to the same escaped form.\"\"\"\n    reference = \"&amp;\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a \" + reference + \" b\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert reference in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_unknown_stays_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-unknown-stays-literal: an unknown entity name is literal text with its ampersand escaped.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"&MadeUpEntity;\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_nul_reference_replaced(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-nul-reference-replaced: the reference for code point zero equals a literal U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, \"&#0;\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, chr(0xFFFD) + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_inert_in_code_span(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-inert-in-code-span: a reference inside a code span is not decoded.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"`&amp;`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;amp;\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Named references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&amp;\", \"&\"),\n        (\"&lt;\", \"<\"),\n        (\"&gt;\", \">\"),\n        (\"&quot;\", '\"'),\n        (\"&copy;\", \"©\"),\n        (\"&AElig;\", \"Æ\"),\n        (\"&nbsp;\", \" \"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_named_reference_decodes_to_its_character(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A recognized named reference yields its character, escaped as text.\"\"\"\n    escaped = {\"&\": \"&amp;\", \"<\": \"&lt;\", \">\": \"&gt;\", '\"': \"&quot;\"}.get(character, character)\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == f\"<p>{escaped}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_with_two_code_points_emits_both(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A named entity that decodes to two code points emits both, in order.\"\"\"\n    assert unescape_and_decode(\"&NotEqualTilde;\") == \"≂̸\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&NotEqualTilde;\\n\") == \"<p>≂̸</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_without_semicolon_is_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A name without its trailing semicolon is not a reference, so the ampersand is test_unknown_name_returns_no_match() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"&MadeUpEntity;\", 0) is None\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_returns_value_and_end() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"x &copy; y\", 2) == (\"©\", 8)\n\n\n# --- Decimal references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&#65;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#0000065;\", \"A\"),\n assert render(project_root, \"&#;\\n\") == \"<p>&amp;#;</p>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Hexadecimal references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&#x41;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#X41;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#x2603;\", \"☃\"),\n        (\"&#x1F600;\", \"\\U0001F600\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_hexadecimal_reference_decodes(project_root: Path, source: str, test_hexadecimal_reference_without_x_is_not_hexadecimal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`&#41;` is decimal, not hexadecimal, so the `4` digit is decimal 41, the `)` character.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#41;\\n\") == \"<p>)</p>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Invalid code points ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"source\",\n    [\n        \"&#0;\",\n        \"&#x0;\",\n test_invalid_code_point_becomes_replacement_character(project_root: Path, source: str) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == \"<p>�</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_last_valid_code_point_is_kept() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"&#x10FFFF;\", 0) == (\"\\U0010FFFF\", 10)\n\n\ndef test_first_code_point_after_surrogates_is_kept() -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#42;foo&#42;\\n\") == \"<p>*foo*</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_decoded_hash_does_not_start_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#35; word\\n\") == (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f24ea800-6ae1-488e-80dd-9351d150839d","uuid":"852ba3c3-cb64-4d67-b01a-db7954bf50b8","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:16:52.748Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_entities.py","oldString":"    assert match_reference(\"&#0000065;\", 0) == (\"A\", 11)","newString":"    assert match_reference(\"&#0000065;\", 0) == (\"A\", 10)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Entity and numeric character reference tests: named references from the HTML5 table, decimal\nand hexadecimal numeric references, U+FFFD replacement, decoded text as plain text, inertness in\ncode spans, and the shared `unescape_and_decode` helper for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\nEach test compares a returned string, a parsed value, or the executable's stdout bytes with its\nexact expected value. The declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import entities\nfrom mdparser.entities import match_reference, unescape_and_decode\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, data: str) -> str:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, data)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_entities_decimal_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-decimal-reference: a decimal reference decodes to the character with the bound code point.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 65\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"x &#\" + str(code_point) + \"; y\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.count(b\"&#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_entities_hex_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-hex-reference: lowercase and uppercase hexadecimal references decode to the same character.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 66\n    lower = \"&#x\" + format(code_point, \"x\") + \";\"\n    upper = \"&#X\" + format(code_point, \"X\") + \";\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, lower + \"\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, upper + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in first.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_named_ampersand(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-named-ampersand: the named ampersand reference round trips to the same escaped form.\"\"\"\n    reference = \"&amp;\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a \" + reference + \" b\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert reference in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_unknown_stays_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-unknown-stays-literal: an unknown entity name is literal text with its ampersand escaped.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"&MadeUpEntity;\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_nul_reference_replaced(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-nul-reference-replaced: the reference for code point zero equals a literal U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, \"&#0;\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, chr(0xFFFD) + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_inert_in_code_span(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-inert-in-code-span: a reference inside a code span is not decoded.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"`&amp;`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;amp;\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Named references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&amp;\", \"&\"),\n        (\"&lt;\", \"<\"),\n        (\"&gt;\", \">\"),\n        (\"&quot;\", '\"'),\n        (\"&copy;\", \"©\"),\n        (\"&AElig;\", \"Æ\"),\n        (\"&nbsp;\", \" \"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_named_reference_decodes_to_its_character(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A recognized named reference yields its character, escaped as text.\"\"\"\n    escaped = {\"&\": \"&amp;\", \"<\": \"&lt;\", \">\": \"&gt;\", '\"': \"&quot;\"}.get(character, character)\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == f\"<p>{escaped}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_with_two_code_points_emits_both(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A named entity that decodes to two code points emits both, in order.\"\"\"\n    assert unescape_and_decode(\"&NotEqualTilde;\") == \"≂̸\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&NotEqualTilde;\\n\") == \"<p>≂̸</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_without_semicolon_is_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A name without its trailing semicolon is not a reference, so the ampersand is escaped.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&copy\\n\") == \"<p>&amp;copy</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_lookup_is_case_sensitive(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`&AMP;` is not The declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import entities\nfrom mdparser.entities import match_reference, unescape_and_decode\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, data: str) -> str:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, data)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_entities_decimal_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-decimal-reference: a decimal reference decodes to the character with the bound code point.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 65\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"x &#\" + str(code_point) + \"; y\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.count(b\"&#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_entities_hex_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-hex-reference: lowercase and uppercase hexadecimal references decode to the same character.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 66\n    lower = \"&#x\" + format(code_point, \"x\") + \";\"\n    upper = \"&#X\" + format(code_point, \"X\") + \";\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, lower + \"\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, upper + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in first.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_named_ampersand(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-named-ampersand: the named ampersand reference round trips to the same escaped form.\"\"\"\n    reference = \"&amp;\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a \" + reference + \" b\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert reference in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_unknown_stays_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-unknown-stays-literal: an unknown entity name is literal text with its ampersand escaped.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"&MadeUpEntity;\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_nul_reference_replaced(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-nul-reference-replaced: the reference for code point zero equals a literal U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, \"&#0;\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, chr(0xFFFD) + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_inert_in_code_span(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-inert-in-code-span: a reference inside a code span is not decoded.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"`&amp;`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;amp;\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Named references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&amp;\", \"&\"),\n        (\"&lt;\", \"<\"),\n        (\"&gt;\", \">\"),\n        (\"&quot;\", '\"'),\n        (\"&copy;\", \"©\"),\n        (\"&AElig;\", \"Æ\"),\n        (\"&nbsp;\", \" \"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_named_reference_decodes_to_its_character(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A recognized named reference yields its character, escaped as text.\"\"\"\n    escaped = {\"&\": \"&amp;\", \"<\": \"&lt;\", \">\": \"&gt;\", '\"': \"&quot;\"}.get(character, character)\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == f\"<p>{escaped}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_with_two_code_points_emits_both(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A named entity that decodes to two code points emits both, in order.\"\"\"\n    assert unescape_and_decode(\"&NotEqualTilde;\") == \"≂̸\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&NotEqualTilde;\\n\") == \"<p>≂̸</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_without_semicolon_is_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A name without its trailing semicolon is not a reference, so the ampersand is escaped.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&copy\\n\") == \"<p>&amp;copy</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_lookup_is_case_sensitive(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`&AMP;` is not in the table, so it stays literal.\"\"\"\n    assert match_reference(\"&AMP;\", 0) is None\n    assert render(project_root, \"&AMP;\\n\") == \"<p>&amp;AMP;</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_unknown_name_returns_no_match() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"&MadeUpEntity;\", 0) is None\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_returns_value_and_end() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"x &copy; y\", 2) == (\"©\", 8)\n\n\n# --- Decimal references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&#65;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#0000065;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#97;\", \"a\"),\n        (\"&#9731;\", \"☃\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_decimal_reference_decodes(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, match_reference(\"&#00000065;\", 0) is None\n    assert match_reference(\"&#0000065;\", 0) == (\"A\", 10)\n\n\ndef test_decimal_reference_with_no_digits_is_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#;\\n\") == \"<p>&amp;#;</p>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Hexadecimal references ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"source\", \"character\"),\n    [\n        (\"&#x41;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#X41;\", \"A\"),\n        (\"&#x2603;\", \"☃\"),\n        (\"&#x1F600;\", \"\\U0001F600\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_hexadecimal_reference_decodes(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == f\"<p>{character}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_hexadecimal_reference_accepts_six_digits_at_most() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A test_hexadecimal_reference_without_x_is_not_hexadecimal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`&#41;` is decimal, not hexadecimal, so the `4` digit is decimal 41, the `)` character.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#41;\\n\") == \"<p>)</p>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Invalid code points ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"source\",\n    [\n        \"&#0;\",\n        \"&#x0;\",\n        \"&#xD800;\",\n        \"&#xDFFF;\",\n        \"&#55296;\",\n        \"&#x110000;\",\n        \"&#1114112;\",\n        \"&#9999999;\",\n    ],\n)\ndef test_invalid_code_point_becomes_replacement_character(project_root: Path, source: str) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == \"<p>�</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_last_valid_code_point_is_kept() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"&#x10FFFF;\", 0) == (\"\\U0010FFFF\", 10)\n\n\ndef test_first_code_point_after_surrogates_is_kept() -> None:\n    assert match_reference(\"&#xE000;\", 0) == (\"\", 8)\n\n\n# --- Decoded characters are plain text ---\n\n\ndef test_decoded_asterisks_do_not_open_emphasis(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#42;foo&#42;\\n\") == \"<p>*foo*</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_decoded_hash_does_not_start_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#35; word\\n\") == \"<p># word</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_decoded_angle_brackets_are_escaped_text(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A decoded `<` is text and not the start of raw HTML.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&lt;b&gt;bold&lt;/b&gt;\\n\") == \"<p>&lt;b&gt;bold&lt;/b&gt;</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_numeric_angle_bracket_is_escaped_text(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert assert render(project_root, \"`&#65;`\\n\") == \"<p><code>&amp;#65;</code></p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_multiple_references_in_one_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert render(project_root, The declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import entities\nfrom mdparser.entities import match_reference, unescape_and_decode\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, data: str) -> str:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, data)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Entities.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_entities_decimal_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-decimal-reference: a decimal reference decodes to the character with the bound code point.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 65\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"x &#\" + str(code_point) + \"; y\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.count(b\"&#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_entities_hex_reference(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-hex-reference: lowercase and uppercase hexadecimal references decode to the same character.\"\"\"\n    code_point = 66\n    lower = \"&#x\" + format(code_point, \"x\") + \";\"\n    upper = \"&#X\" + format(code_point, \"X\") + \";\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, lower + \"\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, upper + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert chr(code_point) in first.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_named_ampersand(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-named-ampersand: the named ampersand reference round trips to the same escaped form.\"\"\"\n    reference = \"&amp;\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a \" + reference + \" b\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert reference in result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_unknown_stays_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-unknown-stays-literal: an unknown entity name is literal text with its ampersand escaped.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"&MadeUpEntity;\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_entities_nul_reference_replaced(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-nul-reference-replaced: the reference for code point zero equals a literal U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    first = run_executable(project_root, \"&#0;\\n\")\n    second = run_executable(project_root, chr(0xFFFD) + \"\\n\")\n    assert first.returncode == 0\n    assert second.returncode == 0\n    assert first.stdout == second.stdout\n\n\ndef test_entities_inert_in_code_span(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC entities-inert-in-code-span: a reference inside a code span is not decoded.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"`&amp;`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"&amp;amp;\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Named references (\"&copy;\", \"©\"),\n        (\"&AElig;\", \"Æ\"),\n        (\"&nbsp;\", \" \"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_named_reference_decodes_to_its_character(project_root: Path, source: str, character: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A recognized named reference yields its character, escaped as text.\"\"\"\n    escaped = {\"&\": \"&amp;\", \"<\": \"&lt;\", \">\": \"&gt;\", '\"': \"&quot;\"}.get(character, character)\n    assert render(project_root, source + \"\\n\") == f\"<p>{escaped}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_named_reference_with_two_code_points_emits_both(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A named test_decimal_digits_are_not_read_as_hexadecimal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`&#41;` is decimal 41, the `)` character, not a hexadecimal reference.\"\"\"\n    assert render(project_root, \"&#41;\\n\") == \"<p>)</p>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Invalid code points ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"source\",\n    [\n        \"&#0;\",\n        \"&#x0;\",\n        \"&#xD800;\",\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1eCNQpPq63SD1ZQvSgF","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Block 8 (entities) is implemented. The full project suite passes, 419 tests, and I did not run the conformance runner because no criterion in this block invokes it.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- `mdparser/entities.py`: added `match_reference`, which decodes HTML5 named references (semicolon-terminated names only, looked up in `html.entities.html5`), 1–7 digit decimal references, and 1–6 digit hex references. Zero, surrogates and values above U+10FFFF become U+FFFD. I also added `unescape_and_decode`, the shared helper for destinations, titles and info strings. The existing `unescape` and `ASCII_PUNCTUATION` are unchanged.\n- `mdparser/inlines.py`: the inline loop now has an `&` branch. A recognized reference is decoded and its character is HTML-escaped as plain text, so `&#42;` cannot open emphasis and `&#35;` cannot start a heading.
